title: Standards spec scorecard
description: MUST/SHOULD/COULD + systems/compliance/effects audit for one registered spec. One scorecard per LOCAL [[spec]] in REGISTRY.a2ml, keyed by spec_id. Hand-authored source; the compliance dashboard is generated from these by scripts/build-scorecards.sh. Serialised as TOML-ish A2ML; this JSON Schema documents the logical shape and is what a validator checks the parsed form against.

spec_id.description: MUST equal the id of a LOCAL [[spec]] in REGISTRY.a2ml.

assessed_date.description: ISO date this assessment was recorded.

assessor.description: Who/what produced the assessment (person, team, or automation id).

must.description: RFC-2119 MUST requirements (load-bearing; a failing MUST is a compliance gap).

should.description: RFC-2119 SHOULD requirements (recommended; a gap is a warning, not a failure).

id.description: Stable id within the scorecard (e.g. M1, S2, C3).

text.description: The requirement, phrased with an RFC-2119 keyword.

system.description: The mechanical check that discharges this requirement: a script path + exit criteria, a CI job name, or the literal 'none'. 'none' is legal but VISIBLE — it is the honest signal that a requirement is asserted but not mechanically enforced. This field drives the dashboard's systems-coverage %.

status.description: pass = system verified it green (evidence REQUIRED). fail = a real, current gap. aspirational = an intentionally-unreachable reach target (e.g. a Grade-A gate); NEVER counted as pass. manual-only = discharged by human/governance judgement, no automatable system (e.g. licence rulings — always manual-only per the Manual-Only licence policy).

evidence.description: REQUIRED when status = pass: the concrete proof (script path + exit criteria, CI job name/url, or issue url). Empty/absent evidence with status=pass is a scorecard defect the generator rejects.

check.description: OPTIONAL executable grounding for a pass: a shell command, run from the repo root, that exits 0 iff the requirement currently holds (e.g. 'bash scripts/spec-checks/k9-svc.sh M4' or a direct test command). Distinct from `system` (human-readable description): `check` is what `build-scorecards.sh --verify` actually RUNS. A pass row with a check is a GROUNDED pass — DYADT applied to the scorecard itself. A pass row without a check remains legal but is reported as self-asserted by --verify. Checks MUST be read-only (no mutation) and MUST NOT touch licence/SPDX content (Manual-Only policy).

effects.description: What is impacted downstream (repos, specs, consumers) if this requirement is unmet — the 'effects' axis of the audit.
